title: His stepmother Sarah and his natural mother Lizetta
summary: His mother in the band was Sarah, his stepmother; his natural mother Lizetta Gray he did not see again until about 1941-42.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You mentioned that your mother played baritone sax -- what was her musical background?

My mother didn't have much of a musical background, just as I think I said earlier -- you couldn't live in the house if you didn't play something, you know, so my dad taught her to play baritone saxophone, you know, she just learned how to play her parts, but I mean, she didn't excell with an instrument.
What was her name?
Her name was Sarah.
S-a-r-a-h?
Uh huh.
What was her maiden name?
Now that's a tough question -- I really don't know; I don't remember that.
When your parents separated, you were 2? Is that right?
I think I was 3 or 3 1/2. Yeah.
And then your father married again, didn't he?
Uh huh. This is the mother I'm speaking of; the one that played saxophone, who was Sarah, who was my stepmother.
Oh.

Who was really the only mother I really knew. Because if someone rears you from the time that you're 3 1/2 until you're an adult, that's the only parent you know, so she was really a wonderful lady, and I say that, you know, don't like to talk about her too much, because she was, really, you know, dear to me. You know? So ... but he really made a good choice -- I don't know about his first choice, but I know his second choice was really a gas.
What was your natural mother's name?

Gray. Her name was Lizetta. Now she was from Louisiana and very fair, and creole type person, you know. I never did see her after I left, when I was 3 1/2. I guess like 1921 ... I don't think I saw her any more until
like, 1941 or '42. That was the first time I'd seen her, you know? So it's kind of, I guess that happens in a lot of families, so that's ...
Lizetta -- was that L-i-z-e-t-t-a, or L-i-s?
No, L-i-z-e-t-t-a. Lizetta. Gray. I remember her name.
Your father and Sarah were married where? In Minneapolis or in New Orleans?
No, I think -- and I'm saying I think -- I think it was Tippeydill, Louisiana. Have you ever heard of Tippeydill?
I think I have.
Yeah, this is what I think ... I think they were in Tippeydill, Louisiana. Yeah, see, that's an area that you know, I would be kind of guessing in that.
